definition: Ratio of soil loss from land under a given cover and management to the loss from continuous bare fallow, under identical slope and rainfall. Near 0 for undisturbed forest / dense litter; near 1 for bare, tilled or fallow soil.

how_to_estimate.summary: Three common routes, in rough order of rigour: (1) a local field- or plot-based C study for your crops and management; (2) a per-land-cover literature lookup (the records below); (3) a continuous estimate from remote sensing - C as a function of fractional vegetation cover or NDVI.

methods.name: literature lookup by land cover
methods.when: no local data; broad land-cover map
methods.notes: Match vegetation form + canopy density + condition + management. Prefer a source in your biome/region.

methods.name: fractional-cover / LAI ratio
methods.notes: C declines exponentially with green + non-green ground cover; gives a continuous C raster. Needs a fractional-cover product.

methods.name: NDVI regression
methods.notes: C = exp(-alpha * NDVI / (beta - NDVI)) type forms; calibrate alpha/beta regionally - transferring them blindly is a known error source.

methods.name: crop-rotation weighting
methods.notes: For arable land, weight crop-specific C by the cropping calendar and modify for tillage, residue and cover crops.

how_to_choose: USLE and RUSLE C are defined slightly differently (RUSLE uses subfactors: prior land use, canopy, surface cover, surface roughness, soil moisture) but values are used interchangeably in practice - note which model your SDR run represents. For a mixed natural class pick by canopy density and litter/ground cover. For cropland, the single biggest control is tillage and residue retention, not the crop: conventional till 0.2-0.5, reduced till 0.15-0.25, no-till + residue 0.05-0.15, no-till + cover crop 0.01-0.08. Record the source_key next to every value you use.

records.caveats: Global class-mean; very low value assumes full canopy + intact litter. Young or thinned stands are much higher.
